items.title: Update all dependencies to their latest releases (links-notation 0.13->0.22, tree-sitter 0.25->0.27, lindera 3->6, 6 more) and enforce freshness in CI
items.body:
## Summary

Every dependency of this repository should be at its latest release (the maintainers' standing requirement, applied first in link-assistant/formal-ai#1169, which also tracks this update as a consumer). `meta-language` 0.58.2 (latest release) and `rust/Cargo.toml` on `main` (checked 2026-09-29) declare nine dependencies whose latest release is outside the declared range:

| Dependency | Declared | Latest release |
|---|---|---|
| `links-notation` | 0.13 | 0.22.0 |
| `tree-sitter` | 0.25.8 | 0.27.0 |
| `tree-sitter-graphql` | 0.1.0 | 0.2.1 |
| `tree-sitter-lua` | 0.2.0 | 0.5.0 |
| `tree-sitter-proto` | 0.4.0 | 0.6.0 |
| `tree-sitter-scala` | 0.25.1 | 0.26.2 |
| `ts-parser-perl` | 1.1.2 | 2.0.0 |
| `doublets` | 0.4.0 | 0.5.0 |
| `lindera` | 3.0.7 | 6.2.0 |

Because of the `links-notation` pin, every consumer that also uses current `links-notation` compiles two copies (0.13.0 and the current one), and Links Notation values cannot flow between `meta-language` networks and the consumer's own `links-notation` types without conversion.

## Requirements

1. R1: update all nine to their latest releases and adapt the code; the tree-sitter 0.27 bump must keep every grammar crate on a compatible `tree-sitter-language` ABI (upgrade the other grammar crates in the same change, and list any grammar that has no 0.27-compatible release as a blocker with its upstream issue).
2. R2: `cargo update` leaves no semver-compatible update pending (`cargo update --dry-run` prints no `Updating` lines).
3. R3: CI job that fails when a direct dependency is behind without an open issue URL on the pin line (`cargo install cargo-outdated --locked && cargo outdated --root-deps-only --exit-code 1`; `npm outdated` for the JavaScript package).
4. R4: publish the release to crates.io and npm.

## How to test

`cargo tree -i links-notation` in a crate depending on the new `meta-language` release and on `links-notation` 0.22 shows a single version; the existing CST round-trip tests pass for every grammar.

items.title: Async functions and await need typed Rust lowering or an explicit async blocker
Provide a no_std ECMAScript tokenizer and a lossless JS/TS <-> link-network pivot for WASM consumers
items.body:
## Summary

Consumers that must parse and render JavaScript/TypeScript in WASM (where tree-sitter grammars do not build) write their own lexer and pivot. link-assistant/formal-ai keeps `rust/src/es_tokenizer.rs` (736 lines: `no_std` ECMAScript tokenizer with regex/division disambiguation and template parts) and `rust/src/es_meta.rs` (863 lines: JS/TS ↔ Links Notation pivot driven by projection rules). This is the same representation job this crate exists for.

## What to do

Provide a `no_std` + `alloc` ECMAScript tokenizer and token-tree ↔ link-network pivot in this crate (a feature or a sibling crate in this repository), lossless for JS and TS source, so every consumer uses one implementation. Related: #195 (full four-language representation; CST by default for all languages).

## How to test

Round trip source → network → source is byte-identical for a corpus of JS/TS files, built for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.


---
Found by a duplication audit of link-assistant/formal-ai against the dependencies its maintainers own (consumer-side tracking: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1182; the audit table there lists the code this issue lets Formal AI delete). Per the organizations' policy, general logic belongs in the dependency so every consumer gets it out of the box and consumer code shrinks.

items.title: Native Node runtime adapters and CommonJS boundaries block JavaScript-to-Rust ports
Finish the remaining issue #195 scope after PR #196: self-translation, native grammars for every language, multi-source merging, interchange, semantics and release
items.body:
## Goal

PR #196 delivers a large part of issue #195: native grammars for 21 languages, executor recovery, shared concepts, decorators, grammar import, export and merge, CI order, and the post-merge release path. It was merged before the work was finished, with the Full Requirements Aggregate still red. This issue lists **everything that still has to be fully delivered**. Each item must be implemented with real behavior, verified by tests in both runtime packages, and recorded in the requirement ledger (`parity/issue-195-requirements.json`). PR #196 was merged as `679a3b3c` on 2026-10-06, and its `Fixes #195` closed #195, although #195 asked to stay open until delivery evidence exists. **This issue carries the whole remaining scope of #195** until every item below is done. It was checked against the #195 body and all 23 maintainer comments on PR #196: about 270 extracted requirements, each mapped to ledger rows and their last evaluated status.

**Fix first:** at merge, the last CI run on `ddcde321` ([run 37530607538](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/37530607538)) failed the JavaScript test `the scope gate reads the full committed ledger after it grows beyond the default subprocess buffer`, so the acceptance stages never ran on the merged head. Make `main` green, then re-run the full evaluation. At PR #196's last fully evaluated run ([run 37503230222](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/37503230222)), every build, test and evidence stage passed. **Full Requirements Aggregate: 306/321**, with 0 gate errors. The 15 open pre-merge rows are listed below. The 5 post-merge rows (section 5) were never evaluated. Their implementation entry points are still `null` in `js/scripts/issue-195-vision-requirements.mjs`, because the code does not exist yet.

The detailed requirements come from PR #196's maintainer comments, which remain authoritative. The main ones:

- [5965533606](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5965533606): CI and release design, native grammars, shared concepts
- [5971613170](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5971613170): JavaScript first, self-translation, decorators, CI order
- [5979473773](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5979473773)
- [5985077141](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5985077141): memory budget and recovery
- [6023909737](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-6023909737): no intentional red; remaining work

---

## 1. Self-translation: JavaScript/TypeScript ↔ Rust through meta-language

**Rows:** `I195-SELF-TRANSLATION-TOOL`, `I195-SELF-TRANSLATION-CARRIED-ZERO`, `I195-SELF-TRANSLATION-SHARED-CORPUS`

**State:**

- Across 119 modules, **26 items are translated and 3,347 carried** (about 0.8 %).
- 16 Rust functions are written, **0 identical** to the hand-written Rust, and 61 of 210 translated lines are shared.
- The last sessions added only small features: string methods, case mapping, trims, `\u` escapes, default parameters and top-level constants.

**To do:**

- [ ] Implement the most frequent carried constructs **in one batch, generically, in JavaScript first**:
  - `export class` and classes, objects and `new`;
  - closures and higher-order functions;
  - destructuring and spread;
  - `Map`/`Set`, iterators and generators;
  - template literals;
  - `try`/`catch`/`throw`;
  - modules, imports and exports;
  - async functions.
- [ ] Bring **carried to 0** for every `js/src` module, with a per-module report published on every CI run.
- [ ] Replace hand-written Rust modules with generated ones, module by module, once they pass `cargo check`, clippy and the shared Links Notation parity corpus. From then on, Rust changes come from translation, not hand-written mirrors.
- [ ] Use decorators to make generated Rust match the project's style. Drive "identical functions" and "shared lines" toward 100 %.
- [ ] Round-trip tests exercise **translated** items, separately from blocks restored from source text by hash:
  - same-language round trips are byte-identical;
  - cross-language round trips preserve behavior.
- [ ] Translate full JavaScript/TypeScript ↔ Rust programs, not only fixtures. Export the capability as a library API and a CLI in both packages.

## 2. Native grammars for every catalog language

**Rows:** `I195-GRAMMAR-NATIVE-MERGED`, `I195-GRAMMAR-LANGUAGE-CATALOG`, `I195-GRAMMAR-LOSSLESS-TREES`, `I195-GRAMMAR-DEPENDENCY-BOUNDARY`, `I195-DEPENDENCY-PRODUCTION-PARSERS-REMOVED`

**State:**

- **Native by default (21):** C, CSV, Diff, Go, GraphQL, INI, Java, JavaScript, JSON, JSON5, Lean, Make, Protocol Buffers, Racket, Regex, Rocq, Rust, Scheme, Solidity, TSX, TypeScript.
- **Bulk matrix:** 67/67 tree-sitter grammars import, 38 accept their sample and 24 match the oracle.
- **29 reject their sample:** Markdown, DOCX, Python, C#, R, Ruby, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Perl, Haskell, OCaml, OCaml Interface, Dart, Agda, CMake, Elixir, Elm, HCL, MATLAB, Nix, Odin, PowerShell, HTML, CSS, YAML, TOML, XML, DTD.

**To do:**

- [ ] **Automatic external-scanner porting.** Most rejections come from missing `scanner.c` behavior; Python, for example, reports `_newline`, `_indent`, `_dedent` and `string_start` as unsupported. Do one of the following, then regenerate all affected languages in one batch:
  - read each pinned `scanner.c` through the native C grammar and translate it into native scanner rules; or
  - implement the common scanner families once, generically: indentation and layout, heredocs, string interpolation, nested comments, raw strings.
- [ ] Every catalog language with a grammar source parses **natively by default** in both runtimes and matches its oracle. It produces a lossless CST (kinds, fields, tokens, trivia, spans, error and missing nodes, embedded languages) and an optional AST with provenance. The trees reload without the source, can be edited, and emit and re-parse.
- [ ] **Remove production tree-sitter.** `web-tree-sitter` is still in `js/package.json` `dependencies`, and `rust/Cargo.toml` still has 36 `tree-sitter*` crates in `[dependencies]`. Keep them only as dev/test oracles. The final production count is **0**, and no vendored grammar binaries are shipped.
- [ ] Changing a native grammar rule changes the public parse result with no host-code patch, and no external engine, subprocess or download runs at parse time.
- [ ] **Built-in formats and grammar-description languages are catalog entries too** ([5895896874](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5895896874)):
  - built-in formats: LiNo, txt, Markdown, PDF and DOCX;
  - grammar-description languages: BNF, EBNF, ABNF, PEG, Peggy, Pest, ANTLR, tree-sitter, Lark, GBNF, Yacc/Bison and lexer specifications.

  Each needs a native Links Notation grammar and tests. **A host-coded parser does not count as native merely because it is called that.**
- [ ] **Natural languages (10 entries).** Define in `docs/vision.md` and the row text what their native representation is, with tests. Every ledger row must have a satisfiable, tested definition; clarify ambiguous rows while keeping their full intent, and never leave a row impossible to pass.
- [ ] Catalog: versions, editions, dialects, aliases, extensions and embedded languages, with every grammar source pinned with license, provenance and independent corpora.

## 3. Real multi-source merging

**Rows:** `I195-MERGE-AUTOMATIC-PIPELINE`, `I195-MERGE-SHIPPED-GRAMMARS-ARE-MERGED`

**State:** reconciliation works: 1,486 shared rules across the 39 languages with two or more sources. But **28 languages have a single source**: Markdown, Lean, Rocq, Python, TSX, Visual Basic, Delphi/Object Pascal, Ruby, Perl, OCaml, OCaml Interface, Bash, Agda, Diff, Elm, Groovy, Make, Nix, PowerShell, Racket, Scheme, four SQL dialects, YAML, DTD and INI.

**To do:**

- [ ] Inventory and import every mature source per language: official specification grammars, grammars-v4, tree-sitter, and the languages' own parsers (Lean, Rocq, the Python PEG grammar and others).
- [ ] A non-interactive pipeline discovers, merges and reconciles the sources into shared concepts, with a reproducible decision report.
- [ ] Shipped grammars are **outputs of the pipeline**, not single-source imports with hand edits.
- [ ] A test fails when a merge only concatenates its sources.

## 4. Other open rows

- [ ] **`I195-ACCEPTANCE-INDEPENDENT-ORACLES`:** each native grammar runs against several independent oracles (tree-sitter, ANTLR, official compilers and provers) on pinned corpora and real projects. Every discrepancy is traced to a test.
- [ ] **`I195-INTERCHANGE-FORMAT-FEATURES`:** every feature of BNF, EBNF, ABNF, PEG, Peggy, Pest, ANTLR, tree-sitter, Lark, GBNF, Yacc/Bison and lexer specifications has a native representation and operational meaning. Imports follow included grammars, lexers, scanners and actions.
- [ ] **`I195-INTERCHANGE-CROSS-FORMAT-TOOLS`:** cross-format and native → external → native cycles run under the actual target tools, installed in CI. Accepted and rejected inputs, structure, precedence, actions and diagnostics are compared.
- [ ] **`I195-SEMANTICS-CONSTRUCT-INVENTORY`:** the full JavaScript, Rust, Lean and Rocq construct inventory (classes, mutation, standard library, imports, async, ownership, macros and notation, types, universes, effects, proofs and tactics) is represented and transformed through the common links. Normal JavaScript is accepted without annotations.
- [ ] **Translation for the full languages, not the portable core.** On `main`, `js/src/translation/emit-common.js` still translates a "checked portable-core program". `ASSUMPTIONS.inBoundsReads` limits agreement to executions whose array reads are in bounds, and the targets abort where JavaScript reads `undefined`. Encode the out-of-bounds behavior faithfully and remove the assumption. Extend all 12 directed translations (JavaScript, Rust, Lean, Rocq), in both packages, to the full languages with project-wide binding, type, universe and effect analysis, macro and notation expansion with hygiene, and proof and tactic elaboration. The passing `I195-SEM-*` and `I195-TRANSLATE-*` rows cover today's fixtures; they must also hold on real projects.
- [ ] **`I195-DOWNSTREAM-TYPESCRIPT-TRANSLATIONS`:** formal-ai's TypeScript ↔ Rust/JavaScript projection pairs translate through shared concepts on clean installed artifacts. A TypeScript CST alone does not count.

## 5. Release

These post-merge rows were never evaluated: `I195-DELIVERY-NPM-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DELIVERY-CRATE-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DELIVERY-RML-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DOWNSTREAM-FORMAL-AI-PUBLISHED` and `I195-ACCEPTANCE-REQUIRED-MERGE-CHECK`.

- [ ] **Publish.** CI on `main` publishes the crate and the npm package from the release tag. npm still serves only `0.46.0`, and the earlier `main` publish failed with `ENEEDAUTH` under OIDC. Document the exact npm trusted-publisher settings the workflow needs, and resolve the continuing publication problem of #171.
- [ ] **Verify the published packages.** Install from npm and crates.io, run the four-language examples from the published packages, and verify checksums and offline-first public APIs. Run RML (PR #184 workloads) and formal-ai against the **published** versions, so that downstream users get the release out of the box.
- [ ] **Merge rule.** Ruleset 24204187, which required Full Requirements Aggregate on `main`, was removed so that PR #196 could merge. Once the pre-merge rows pass, re-create a rule that requires the PR checks on the default branch. Its post-merge report on `main` verifies it with data the workflow token can read.
- [ ] **Dependency freshness.** The scheduled job on `main` keeps every retained dependency current (see #197). Resolve the Rocq/OCaml toolchain and build-image constraints with a reproducible solution: "held by another dependency" describes work to do, not a reason to stay behind.
- [ ] **Memory regression checks.** Each memory fix (the parse memo budget, lazy grammar loading, reuse of the inline Markdown parser, compact offset maps, streamed parity evidence) has a bounded-heap or peak-RSS regression check in CI. Where formal-ai's workloads blew past their memory limit, record the cause and keep its regression test.

---

## Rules for whoever works on this (people and AI agents)

1. **Every session delivers real implementation progress** on the items above. A red check means unfinished work to implement now. It is never intended, never a reason to stop, and never a reason to weaken, skip or re-classify a requirement.
2. **Work in bulk, not one small feature per session.** Pick a whole item, such as the next batch of carried constructs or automatic scanner porting, and finish it.
3. **JavaScript first.** Develop and debug in JavaScript; port to Rust in one batch, by self-translation wherever possible. Never mirror commit by commit.
4. **Automate:** importers, merging, scanner porting, the translator and generators, instead of hand-writing grammars or Rust. Make each fix generic, then regenerate everything it affects.
5. **Bulk pushes.** Draft the whole batch, commit locally, re-read the diff, then push once. While CI runs, continue with the next item, and fix every reported failure in one batch.
6. **CI** stays as designed:
   - JavaScript runs first, and Rust and acceptance only after it passes;
   - every failure is reported in one run;
   - only pre-merge checks run on pull requests;
   - `main` produces the release.
7. **Resources.** Earlier sessions were killed for running out of memory.
   - Locally, run only targeted JavaScript tests, plus one `cargo check` when porting, with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 RUST_TEST_THREADS=2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, wrapped in `node scripts/with-cache-cleanup.mjs`.
   - Never run locally: the full suites, acceptance, coverage, the bulk pipeline, self-translation reports, the formal-ai or RML workloads, or whole-corpus experiments.
   - Run `node scripts/clean-caches.mjs` after each batch, kill leftover `cargo`, `rustc`, `node`, `lean` and `rocq` processes, and commit early.
8. Split this issue into smaller pull requests per item if that helps. Every pull request must be green before merge.

Related: #195, #196. Also #197 (dependency updates and freshness) and #198 (no_std ECMAScript tokenizer and lossless JS/TS ↔ link-network pivot), which overlap with sections 1, 2 and 5.

items.title: fix: runtime translation parity, grammar imports and acceptance CI
items.body:
This draft continues issue #199 and the remaining issue #195 requirements. It corrects runtime translation differences, native pattern import failures, and CI defects that prevented acceptance evidence from being collected. The full issue scope remains open.

- Preserve binding and parameter-default metadata in Rust stages, evaluate omitted defaults in the defining scope, and align Unicode diagnostics and source spans. Generate the shared translation helpers from JavaScript with Links decorators and check regeneration.
- Compile character-class intersection, difference and symmetric difference to native Links operations, with range/union precedence, left association and outer negation. Support fixed-width and braced hexadecimal scalar escapes and include ASCII keycap bases in emoji classes. The importer now compiles the complete Swift identifier pattern.
- Generate 27 shared pattern fixtures through the existing native importer. Both packages execute the same Links data over all 128 ASCII characters and selected Unicode, astral, nested, empty-set and repeated inputs. Rust compares the outcomes with the pinned regex crate as an independent test oracle. These finite checks do not establish complete Unicode binary-property or Swift syntax-tree coverage.
- Compile byte-identical Rust round-trip fixtures with rustc and require warning-free Clippy output for generated Rust. Preserve the original fixtures and test that generated warnings still fail.
- Verify RML PR184's pinned 17-workload inventory from immutable, blob-checked GitHub source during pre-merge acceptance. Keep live-head drift checking as a non-blocking report on main, with explicit pull-request exclusion. Preserve RML structure profiles in both whole-network reuse probes.
- Verify portable report identities, exact commits, source hashes and the complete 120-module published inventory before recording observations. Register the generators, refresh shipped concept data, and keep Rust modules within the existing size limit.
- Install JavaScript report dependencies before Rust checks. Keep every fresh-merge test and its 20-minute deadline; optimize parsing with debug and overflow checks, clean build binaries, and cache registry sources.

Reproduction: before this batch, `[a-z&&[^aeiou]]` and Swift's identifier pattern were reported as unsupported; braced hexadecimal escapes also failed. Run `node experiments/inspect-native-character-classes.mjs` to compare the finite corpus with the preceding commit. The original translation-stage mismatch reproduces with `cd rust && cargo test --test unit translation_stages`.

Validation: 59 focused JavaScript tests pass, together with the Rust character-class corpus and independent oracle. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo check --all-targets --all-features` pass with bounded build parallelism. Earlier focused translation, stage, default, Unicode, report, consumer-profile, workflow and native-compiler regressions pass. Online source verification, naming, documentation, parity, dependency inventory, fixture regeneration and ledger checks pass. All 326 existing requirement rows and 406 fixture definitions are preserved; two atomic rows were added, for 328 rows and 408 fixture identities.

Latest head: `29719c86dad4c91f2caca5f67662f83b5ebfc8fb`. [CI run 37679053977](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/37679053977), created 2026-10-07 20:02:45 UTC, is pending. The preceding batch passed all ordinary JavaScript groups, all Rust platform test groups, coverage, packaging, four native stages, pinned RML workloads and all three clean-consumer platforms before this push; Formal AI was still running. Those observations belong to the preceding commit.

The remaining obligations include zero-carried bulk self-translation, native merged grammars across the catalog, production parser removal, complete lossless trees, automatic multi-source merging, independent grammar-tool conformance, the full four-language semantic construct inventory, downstream TypeScript translations and published delivery. The ledger still contains 13 rows with null implementation entry points. This PR stays draft until the aggregate verifies all required evidence.

items.title: docs.rs builds fail for meta-language and all its dependents: non-optional lindera dependency
items.body:
## Summary

`meta-language` depends on `lindera` non-optionally, and `lindera`'s build script fails on docs.rs. As a result **`meta-language`'s own documentation does not build**, and neither does the documentation of every crate that depends on it.

- `meta-language` 0.45.0 on docs.rs: *All builds failed* (build 3577282)
- `formal-ai` 0.296.0, which depends on `meta-language`: *All builds failed* ([build 3868612](https://docs.rs/crate/formal-ai/0.296.0/builds))

Bisected: `formal-ai` 0.183.0 builds green on docs.rs, 0.184.0 fails. The only dependency change between those two releases was adding `meta-language`.

## Root cause (upstream of here)

`lindera-dictionary/src/assets.rs` has two bugs in the branch guarded by `DOCS_RS`, which make docs.rs builds of `lindera-jieba` fail unconditionally: the dummy dictionary is scaffolded into `input_dir/` while the builder reads `input_dir/dict-src/`, and `fs::create_dir` is not idempotent so any build-script re-run in a reused `OUT_DIR` fails with `File exists (os error 17)`.

Reported with a full reproduction and a suggested patch: lindera/lindera#750.

```
error: failed to run custom build command for `lindera-jieba v3.0.7`
  Error: LinderaError { kind: Io, source: Failed to create dummy input directory:
  ".../mecab-jieba-0.1.1" Caused by: File exists (os error 17) }
```

## Why this needs an action here too

**Upgrading lindera does not fix it.** I checked `lindera-dictionary` 4.0.0 — the newest version on crates.io — and it carries the identical `fs::create_dir` at `assets.rs:286`. So bumping the pin from `^3.0.7` to `4.x` changes nothing for docs.rs.

**Dependents cannot work around it.** Because the `lindera` dependency is not optional, a crate depending on `meta-language` has no feature to switch off, and `[package.metadata.docs.rs]` cannot reach into a transitive build script. The failure is inescapable from downstream.

## Reproducible example

```toml
[dependencies]
meta-language = "0.45.0"
```

```bash
cargo install cargo-docs-rs
cargo docs-rs
# or, minimally, reproduce the underlying build-script failure directly:
#   cargo new jieba-repro && cd jieba-repro
#   cargo add lindera-jieba@4.0.0 --no-default-features --features embed-jieba
#   DOCS_RS=1 cargo build && DOCS_RS=1 cargo build
```

## Suggested fix

Put `lindera` behind a feature so dependents that do not need the tokenizer can opt out — which also restores their docs.rs builds today, without waiting on the upstream fix:

```toml
[dependencies]
lindera = { version = "3.0.7", default-features = false, features = ["embed-jieba"], optional = true }

[features]
default = ["lindera"]      # keep current behaviour for existing users
lindera = ["dep:lindera"]
```

Dependents would then use `meta-language = { version = "...", default-features = false }` when they do not need tokenization.

Optionally also add to `Cargo.toml` so the failure is visible here rather than only in dependents:

```toml
[package.metadata.docs.rs]
all-features = false
```

## Workaround

Until either this or lindera/lindera#750 lands, dependents' docs.rs pages stay red with no action available to them.

## Context

Found while fixing CI/CD false positives and failures in `formal-ai` ([link-assistant/formal-ai#736](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/736)); the full analysis is in that repository's case study for the issue. Happy to open a PR here for the feature-gating if that is the direction you would prefer.

items.title: feat: implement the issue 195 capabilities and their acceptance evidence
items.body:
**Status: not complete.** Latest: ddcde32 makes `trim`/`trimStart`/`trimEnd` and `\u` escapes portable into Rust, and bd519c2 registers the second identical re-post of the audit; 882c70f makes string `toLowerCase`/`toUpperCase` portable into Rust (Lean and Rocq refuse them with a reason); e111ba9 makes default parameters and top-level constants portable (tests/translation-defaults.test.js); b8397c4 registers the [re-posted bulk-delivery audit](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-6024489303); 87dba40 registers the [c39470d0 audit](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-6023909737); ebe3b43 makes string `startsWith`/`endsWith`/`includes` portable in every target (tests/translation-strings.test.js), the first step on the self-translation carried constructs. The issue #195 directive is unfinished, and this PR stays a draft until every requirement is implemented. Every PR check must pass. A red check is a defect to fix now; unfinished requirements are work to implement, not a reason for red CI. The open implementation rows are listed in the [path to a green PR and a release](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5965533606): the native grammars of the catalog languages with executor recovery, shared concept records, the interchange format tools, the automatic merge pipeline, the construct inventory, removing tree-sitter from production, the TypeScript downstream translations and the independent oracles.

The authoritative [vision](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/issue-195-cc10e17ab860/docs/vision.md) and [atomic ledger](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/issue-195-cc10e17ab860/parity/issue-195-requirements.json) define the scope: **326 requirements**. No existing row, expected behavior, assertion, fixture, runtime or alias was removed or weakened.

## Latest updates

- **Solidity native by default in both runtimes, with tree-sitter-solidity a development oracle only (044f66c..1a5f5db).**
  - **Solidity parses natively (`I195-GRAMMAR-NATIVE-SOLIDITY`, 044f66c).** `parity/grammars/native/solidity.lino` is a merged grammar imported from the pinned tree-sitter-solidity 1.2.13 grammar. The JavaScript executor builds the oracle rows of every corpus source, rejects the input the oracle recovers from and keeps every byte.
  - **Readable names and shared concepts (667ad0d).** Rules get readable names (`signed_integer_type`, `unsigned_integer_type`, `fixed_point_type`, `unsigned_fixed_point_type`, `yul_built_in_function`). True and false values, parameters, declaration bodies, call arguments and map types are merged into the shared concepts. - **API (both runtimes).**
  - `mergeGrammars` / `merge_grammars` groups sources by language and edition. It merges two rules only when a recursive structural proof shows the definitions are equivalent: references are compared up to consistent renaming, including recursive and mutually recursive rules. Each merge is recorded as a justified decision.
  - Name similarity and identical sample parses only *nominate* candidates. Unproven candidates stay separate as explicit `uncertain-match` alternatives.
  - Same-named rules with different meanings (homonyms) are kept apart under source-qualified names.
  - An unresolved `requiredEquivalences` pair is a failure, and `assertMergeComplete` / `assert_merge_complete` rejects it.
- **Determinism and incremental re-merge.**
  - The output, including its SHA-256 fingerprint, is byte-identical across runs.
  - Merging is idempotent, and reordering the sources or their rules does not change the result.
  - Passing the previous result re-merges only the groups whose sources changed.
  - Conflicts are resolved by the recorded source precedence. Language and edition boundaries are never crossed.
- **Binding-aware rename.** `renameGrammarRule` / `rename_grammar_rule` rewrites the definition and every reference, including recursive, qualified (`namespace::rule`) and reloaded ones, and keeps the source aliases.
  - It rejects invalid names, unknown rules and collisions.
  - Labeled captures are not renamed.

The generated-parser tests picked the lexicographically first artifact, which failed with E0514 under 1.99.

items.title: Cross-format document reconstruction & round-trip translation (reconstruct_text_as for Markdown/HTML/PDF/DOCX/txt)
items.body:
## Cross-format document reconstruction & round-trip translation

### Context
Required by [`link-assistant/formal-ai#425`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/425)
/ [PR #432](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/432#issuecomment-4700133344):

> if we have 1 to 1 match of concept in both languages/data formats we can
> easily translate them … just converting them to meta-language and back will
> allow translation from Markdown/PDF/Docs to meta-language and back.

### Current state
`reconstruct_text_as()` exists but targets natural-/programming-language
reconstruction via `translation_rules`; there are no translation rule sets or
syntax mappings for the **document markup/binary formats**, so a document parsed
from one format cannot be reconstructed as another (e.g. DOCX → Markdown).

### Requested
Make `reconstruct_text_as("Markdown" | "HTML" | "PDF" | "DOCX" | "txt", …)` work
over the shared formatting concept layer (#83), so a document parsed from
any supported format reconstructs into any other when the source uses only
concepts both formats support. Use the existing `LanguageProfile` mechanism to
flag features the target cannot represent (e.g. nested tables → plain text) as
documented lossy fallbacks rather than silent data loss.

### Acceptance
- Round-trip matrix fixtures: for each ordered pair in {txt, Markdown, HTML, PDF, DOCX}, a sample using common concepts (bold/italic/heading/paragraph/list/link) survives `A → concepts → B → concepts → A`.
- `LanguageProfile` reports unsupported concepts per target with a defined fallback.
- README documents the cross-format translation entry point and the per-format fidelity matrix.

### Dependencies
Blocked by #83; consumes #84 (PDF) and #85 (DOCX).

items.title: `LinkNetwork::parse` is O(nodes × bytes): `point_at_byte` rescans the whole source for every span
items.body:
**Version:** reproduced on `meta-language` 0.54.0 and 0.58.1 (latest).

## What happens

Every node conversion resolves its byte offsets to a `(row, column)` `Point`, and
that resolution walks the source from byte 0 each time. `src/tree_sitter_adapter.rs`
(0.58.1, line 374):

```rust
fn point_at_byte(text: &str, byte: usize) -> Point {
    let mut row = 0;
    let mut line_start = 0;
    for (index, value) in text.bytes().enumerate().take(byte) {
        if value == b'\n' {
            row += 1;
            line_start = index + 1;
        }
    }
    Point::new(row, byte - line_start)
}
```

It is called twice per span (line 366):

```rust
fn span_for_range(text: &str, start: usize, end: usize, offset: SpanOffset) -> SourceSpan {
    SourceSpan::new(
        ByteRange::new(offset.byte + start, offset.byte + end),
        offset.point(point_at_byte(text, start)),
        offset.point(point_at_byte(text, end)),
    )
}
```

and `span_for_range` is reached from `span_for_node`, `insert_leaf_token` and
`insert_gap_token` — i.e. once per node and once per token, for every node in the
tree. Each call is `O(byte)`, so a full parse is `O(nodes × bytes)`: quadratic in
file size, since node count grows linearly with bytes.

## Reproduction

A standalone crate with `meta-language` as its only dependency. It parses the
same synthetic Rust module at growing sizes and prints nanoseconds per byte — a
linear parser holds that column flat; a quadratic one doubles it every time the
input doubles.

```toml
[package]
name = "meta-language-quadratic-parse"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
meta-language = "0.58.1"
```

```rust
use std::time::Instant;

use meta_language::{LinkNetwork, ParseConfiguration};

fn unit(index: usize) -> String {
    format!(
        "/// Doc comment for item {index}.\n\
         pub fn item_{index}(input: &str) -> usize {{\n\
         \x20   let trimmed = input.trim();\n\
         \x20   if trimmed.is_empty() {{\n\
         \x20       return {index};\n\
         \x20   }}\n\
         \x20   trimmed.len() + {index}\n\
         }}\n\n"
    )
}

fn main() {
    println!("{:>6}  {:>9}  {:>10}  {:>14}", "units", "bytes", "parse ms", "ns per byte");
    for units in [64_usize, 128, 256, 512, 1024] {
        let source: String = (0..units).map(unit).collect();
        let started = Instant::now();
        let network = LinkNetwork::parse(&source, "rust", ParseConfiguration::default());
        let elapsed = started.elapsed();
        assert_eq!(network.reconstruct_text(), source);
        let bytes = source.len();
        let per_byte = elapsed.as_nanos() as f64 / bytes as f64;
        println!("{units:>6}  {bytes:>9}  {:>10}  {per_byte:>14.0}", elapsed.as_millis());
    }
}
```

Measured with `cargo run --release` (the *favourable* case — optimisations on):

| units | bytes | parse ms | ns per byte |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | 11 416 | 86 | 7 615 |
| 128 | 22 984 | 312 | 13 593 |
| 256 | 46 408 | 1 115 | 24 032 |
| 512 | 93 256 | 4 262 | 45 710 |
| 1 024 | 187 048 | 18 168 | 97 134 |

Doubling the input multiplies the total time by ~3.6–3.8 and the per-byte cost
by ~1.8–1.9 at every step — the signature of an `O(n²)` term dominating. A
linear parser would hold the last column flat.

The same measurement on the `dev` profile — the profile a test suite runs
under, and the one that produced the CI failure below — scales identically and
is roughly 25× slower in absolute terms:

| units | bytes | parse ms | ns per byte |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | 11 416 | 2 167 | 189 902 |
| 128 | 22 984 | 8 263 | 359 539 |
| 256 | 46 408 | 33 223 | 715 893 |
| 512 | 93 256 | 127 817 | 1 370 607 |
| 1 024 | 187 048 | 503 302 | 2 690 767 |

## Attribution

Sampled with `gdb -p <pid> -batch -ex "bt 80"` against a process parsing a
39 KB Rust module. **12 of 12 samples** were inside `point_at_byte`, called from
`span_for_range` → `convert_node` → `network_from_tree` → `LinkNetwork::parse`.

## Impact

A 39 KB Rust module takes **over ten seconds** to parse on the `dev` profile.
In our case (`link-assistant/formal-ai`, issue
[#1017](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1017)) that parse sat
behind a lookup on the request path, so a server's *first* HTTP response took
~13 s and two macOS CI slices hit the integration harness's 30-second timeout.
Any consumer that parses a real source file inside a request, a language server,
or a watch loop will meet the same wall.

## Suggested fix

Compute the line-start table **once per parse** and binary-search it, which turns
each lookup into `O(log lines)` and the parse into `O(nodes × log lines)`:

```rust
/// Byte offset of the first character of each line, ascending. `line_starts[0]`
/// is always 0, so the table is never empty and the search below always hits.
fn line_starts(text: &str) -> Vec<usize> {
    let mut starts = vec![0];
    starts.extend(
        text.bytes()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|(_, value)| *value == b'\n')
            .map(|(index, _)| index + 1),
    );
    starts
}

fn point_at_byte(line_starts: &[usize], byte: usize) -> Point {
    // The index of the last line start at or before `byte`.
    let row = line_starts.partition_point(|start| *start <= byte) - 1;
    Point::new(row, byte - line_starts[row])
}
```

The table belongs next to `text` in `ConvertContext`, built once in
`network_from_tree` (and once per embedded/injected region, alongside the
existing `SpanOffset`), so no call site needs to own it. `line_starts` is
`O(bytes)` once, versus `O(bytes)` per node today.

Two smaller wins are available on top:

* `span_for_node` can take `node.start_position()` / `node.end_position()`
  straight from tree-sitter, which already tracks points during parsing — no
  lookup at all for the node case.
* `span_for_range(text, start, end, …)` resolves `end` from scratch after
  resolving `start`; with the table that no longer matters, but scanning
  forward from `start` would also have removed the worst of it.

## Workaround for consumers

Until this lands, avoid parsing on any latency-sensitive path, and memoise
parses of build-time-constant sources. That is what we did:
[`link-assistant/formal-ai#1018`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1018)
proves a cache lookup will miss *before* building the artifact that parses, and
memoises the one round-trip whose input is a compile-time constant. It removed
the timeout (first response ~13 s → ~0.3 s) without touching the algorithm —
which is why the algorithmic fix still belongs here.

items.title: Easy grammar extensibility and grammar inference

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
We should allow to easily develop grammars inherited from meta-language, by using grammar inference (find patterns in examples of texts of that grammar).

Ideally it should be possible to reconstruct programming language grammar by using only examples of correct programming language texts.

We also need to make sure we use https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-notation as a basis for our meta-language. And our meta language itself is inherited from meta-notation.

So when constructing new grammars in meta-language ecosystem, it should be possible to have maximum freedom of grammar inference.

Search online best papers on the topic of grammar inference, and we need to have working rust implementation, that is able to generate grammar description in the meta-language itself, which after that we should be able to translate to rust, javascript and other languages (we also should include of PEG, BNF and other languages, to be parsed as meta language).

Note that meta language has shared concepts between all the languages, so if the concept is exactly the same in both of formal or natural languages, it will be possible to translate it 1 to 1 with little code modification or extension.

We need to plan as much issues as possible to make sure our system fully implements everything, beats all the competitors in all metrics.

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

You have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until everything is totally planned as issues in this repository.

Make sure all issues are sub-issues of this issue, and have properly configured blocked by relationships using gh tool, to make dependencies between issues visible.

Each issue should be maximum detailed possible, so even week AI agent will be able to complete it.

items.title: Port competitor test corpora (wave 2), extend parity targets, and ratchet a coverage gate
items.body:
## Context

Issue #47: "We should have 100% tests coverage, which should copy most of test
cases from our competitors in each sector/scope" and "We should check that
nothing is deferred or left unimplemented in our vision and roadmap." Today 48
provenanced `PARITY_FIXTURES` exist (a small fraction of upstream suites), the
`cargo llvm-cov` job enforces no threshold, and `docs/parity-roadmap.md` still
defers SQL dialect and Delphi-specific coverage. See
[`requirements.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-47/requirements.md) **R-19**/**R-20** and
[`solution-plans.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-47/solution-plans.md) **S-15**.

**Blocked by:** `#02`, `#08`, `#12`, `#14` - this is the closing gate over the
features those issues add.

## Scope

- Port the five highest-value suites identified in
  [`competitors-code-tooling.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-47/competitors-code-tooling.md):
  Coccinelle `tests/` (`.c`/`.cocci`/`.res` transform triples), tree-sitter
  `test/corpus` + core `test/fixtures/error_corpus`, Semgrep
  `tests/patterns/<lang>/`, srcML `test/parser/testsuite` lossless round-trip
  cases, LibCST adversarial whitespace fixtures (runner-up: babel-parser
  fixtures). Sample per construct where suites are huge; document sampling so
  nothing reads as "covered everything" when it is not.
- Extend `PARITY_TARGETS` with the surveyed projects not yet tracked:
  ast-grep, Semgrep, Comby, GritQL, srcML, difftastic, Babel, SWC,
  OpenRewrite, Spoon, JavaParser, Rascal, Stratego/Spoofax, TXL, MPS,
  Coccinelle; GF, Universal Dependencies, LanguageTool from the
  natural-language survey; doublets-rs and links-notation storage gates.
- Ratchet coverage: record the current `cargo llvm-cov` line coverage, fail
  CI below the floor, raise the floor with each wave toward 100%.
- Roadmap audit (R-19): every deferral in `docs/parity-roadmap.md` is either
  implemented or tracked by an open issue with a link.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each new parity target has provenanced, license-recorded fixtures and
      capability gates, like existing targets.
- [ ] Ported corpora include both round-trip and transform-expectation cases.
- [ ] CI fails when coverage drops below the recorded floor.
- [ ] Roadmap contains no untracked deferral.
- [ ] Changelog fragment added (`bump: minor`).

## References

- Requirement: [`requirements.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-47/requirements.md) R-19, R-20
- Solution: [`solution-plans.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-47/solution-plans.md) S-15
- Part of #47; work lands on branch `issue-47-76af108c0f24` (PR #48).

---

items.title: Add natural-language segmentation and identification
items.body:
Fixes #9.

### Summary
- Adds a natural-language annotation layer over existing lossless text parses for the 10 natural-language targets.
- Emits region-scoped Language, Semantic, and word Token links without changing stored source bytes.
- Adds detector configuration with Lingua as the default backend and Whatlang as the alternative.

### Implementation
- Uses `lingua` for default language identification, `whatlang` when configured, `unicode-segmentation` for non-CJK word segmentation, and `lindera` Jieba segmentation for Mandarin.
- Annotates NFC/NFD normalization stability and bidi direction as Semantic links over the existing source span.
- Adds the NLP dependencies with required language features plus a minor changelog fragment.
- Initializes the Windows MSVC environment, configures AWS-LC CMake settings, and pins Cargo's Windows MSVC linker to Visual Studio `link.exe` so Git for Windows `link.exe` cannot shadow it during the transitive Lindera Jieba build.

### Reproduction Tests
- `natural_language_parse_adds_segmentation_language_and_unicode_annotations` covers Latin segmentation, Mandarin `你好。` segmentation, and Arabic bidi/normalization annotations.
- `natural_language_identifier_backend_is_switchable` verifies the configurable Whatlang detector path.
- `natural_language_fixtures_keep_byte_exact_reconstruction_with_language_regions` verifies all 10 natural-language fixtures reconstruct byte-for-byte and get region-scoped Language links.
- `windows_test_job_configures_aws_lc_cmake_before_running_tests` guards the Windows workflow setup needed by the new Lindera dependency chain, including the explicit Cargo MSVC linker path.

### Local Verification

items.title: [E1] CLI: infer/import/emit/translate-grammar
items.body:
> **Part of #93** — _Easy grammar extensibility and grammar inference_. Filed from the
> maximally-detailed case-study spec [`E1-cli-grammar-subcommands.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/E1-cli-grammar-subcommands.md).
>
> **Blocked by:** #95 (A1), #99 (B1), #106 (C1), #118 (D5)
>
> _Dependencies are also wired natively (GitHub sub-issue of #93 + `blocked_by`)._

---

# E1 — CLI: infer / import / emit / translate-grammar

> **Epic:** E — Tooling, integration, benchmarking · **Blocked by:** [`A1`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/A1-grammar-ir.md), [`B1`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/B1-bnf-importer.md), [`C1`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/C1-bnf-ebnf-abnf-emitters.md), [`D5`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/D5-blackbox-cfg-inference.md)
> **Requirements:** P-1, P-7 · **Milestone:** M5
> Part of the issue #93 grammar-extensibility & inference initiative. Background:
> [`solution-plans.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/solution-plans.md) §Epic E,
> [`existing-capabilities.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/existing-capabilities.md) §1 (the CLI scaffold).

## Context

The whole grammar subsystem — IR (A1), importers (B1–B7), emitters (C1–C3, C7),
inference (D5) — is library-only until it is reachable from the command line.
P-1 ("easy to develop new grammars") and P-7 ("working Rust implementation")
require a usable tool, not just a crate API. Today `src/main.rs` exposes exactly
two `clap` subcommands — `Describe` and `Verify { language, text }`
(`src/main.rs:15-37`) — wired through `clap::{Parser, Subcommand}`
(`src/main.rs:1, 5-13`) and documented in `README.md` §CLI
(`cargo run -- describe`, `cargo run -- verify …`). There is **no CLI for
inference or grammar translation** (gap recorded in
[`existing-capabilities.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/existing-capabilities.md) §3, row E1).

This issue adds four subcommands on that same scaffold — `infer`,
`import-grammar`, `emit-grammar`, `translate-grammar` — each a thin shell over an
existing library entry point. It follows the existing `describe`/`verify` style
exactly: a `Command` enum variant with `#[arg(long)]` flags, a small free
function per command, dispatched from `match cli.command`.

## Goal

Add four `clap` subcommands to `src/main.rs` so a user can, from the shell:
infer a grammar from example texts (D5), import a grammar from any supported
notation into the A1 IR / LiNo (B1–B7), emit an A1 grammar to any supported
notation (C1–C3, C7), and translate a grammar's human-facing surface across
natural languages (C6) — each with explicit flags, defaults, examples, and a
documented output format, matching the established `describe`/`verify` style.

## Scope

**In scope**
- Four new `Command` variants in `src/main.rs` and their handler functions.
- Argument parsing/validation via `clap` derive (`--format`, `--strategy`,
  `--metrics`, `--out`, `--start`, `--key`, `--from-language`/`--to-language`,
  positional input paths) with sensible defaults and clear `--help` text.
- Reading example files/dirs for `infer`; reading a grammar file for the others.
- Printing the result to stdout (or `--out <path>`) and a non-zero exit on error
  (mirroring `verify`'s `std::process::exit(1)`, `src/main.rs:53`).
- README §CLI updated with the new subcommands and examples.

**Out of scope** (owned elsewhere — E1 only *calls* them)
- The inference engine itself → **D5** (and D1–D9). E1 calls `infer_grammar(...)`.
- The importers → **B1–B7**. E1 calls `import_bnf(...)` etc.
- The emitters → **C1–C3, C7**. E1 calls `emit_bnf(...)` etc.
- Cross-language translation logic → **C6**. E1 calls the C6 entry point.
- Registering an inferred grammar as a live parser → **E2** (E1 may print a hint
  that `parse_with_registry` is available, but does not own that path).
- End-to-end example programs under `examples/` → **E5**.

## Design / specification

Extend the existing enum (do not restructure `Cli`; keep `Describe`/`Verify`):

```rust
#[derive(Subcommand, Debug)]
enum Command {
    /// Print the built-in self-description roots.            (existing)
    Describe,
    /// Parse text into a lossless token network and verify.  (existing)
    Verify { /* language, text — src/main.rs:20-27 */ },

    /// Infer a grammar from example texts (D5).
    Infer {
        /// One or more files or directories of example texts.
        #[arg(required = true)]
        examples: Vec<std::path::PathBuf>,
        /// Output grammar notation.
        #[arg(long, value_enum, default_value_t = GrammarFormatArg::Lino)]
        format: GrammarFormatArg,
        /// Inference strategy / pipeline depth.
        #[arg(long, value_enum, default_value_t = StrategyArg::Auto)]
        strategy: StrategyArg,
        /// Also print precision/recall/F1/runtime (D1 metrics) to stderr.
        #[arg(long)]
        metrics: bool,
        /// Write the grammar here instead of stdout.
        #[arg(long)]
        out: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    },

    /// Import a grammar in another notation into the IR / LiNo (B1–B7).
    ImportGrammar {
        /// Source notation of the input file.
        #[arg(long, value_enum)]
        format: ImportFormatArg, // bnf|ebnf|abnf|peg|antlr|lark|gbnf|tree-sitter
        /// Grammar file to import.
        #[arg(required = true)]
        input: std::path::PathBuf,
        /// Output notation for the imported grammar (default LiNo).
        #[arg(long, value_enum, default_value_t = GrammarFormatArg::Lino)]
        to: GrammarFormatArg,
        #[arg(long)]
        out: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    },

    /// Emit an IR/LiNo grammar to another notation (C1–C3, C7).
    EmitGrammar {
        /// Target notation.
        #[arg(long, value_enum)]
        format: EmitFormatArg, // bnf|ebnf|abnf|peg|gbnf|tree-sitter
        /// Grammar file (IR/LiNo) to emit from.
        #[arg(required = true)]
        input: std::path::PathBuf,
        #[arg(long)]
        out: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    },

    /// Translate a grammar's human-facing surface across languages (C6).
    TranslateGrammar {
        /// Grammar file (IR/LiNo) to translate.
        #[arg(required = true)]
        input: std::path::PathBuf,
        /// Source natural language (e.g. en).
        #[arg(long)]
        from_language: String,
        /// Target natural language (e.g. ru).
        #[arg(long)]
        to_language: String,
        #[arg(long)]
        out: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    },
}
```

`GrammarFormatArg` / `ImportFormatArg` / `EmitFormatArg` / `StrategyArg` are
`#[derive(ValueEnum)]` enums that map 1-to-1 onto A1's `GrammarFormat`
(`MetaLanguage, Bnf, Ebnf, Abnf, Peg, Antlr, Lark, Gbnf, TreeSitter, Inferred` —
A1 §Design) plus a `Lino` surface option. Keep the import/emit variants scoped to
formats whose importer/emitter exists at M5 (`bnf` via [`B1`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/B1-bnf-importer.md)
and `emit_bnf`/`emit_ebnf`/`emit_abnf` via [`C1`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/C1-bnf-ebnf-abnf-emitters.md)
are the hard dependencies; gate not-yet-implemented formats behind a clear
"unsupported format" error rather than a panic, and widen as B2–B7 / C2–C3 / C7
land).

Dispatch mirrors `src/main.rs:33-37`:

```rust
match cli.command {
    Command::Describe => describe(),
    Command::Verify { language, text } => verify(&language, &text),
    Command::Infer { examples, format, strategy, metrics, out } =>
        infer(&examples, format, strategy, metrics, out.as_deref()),
    Command::ImportGrammar { format, input, to, out } =>
        import_grammar(format, &input, to, out.as_deref()),
    Command::EmitGrammar { format, input, out } =>
        emit_grammar(format, &input, out.as_deref()),
    Command::TranslateGrammar { input, from_language, to_language, out } =>
        translate_grammar(&input, &from_language, &to_language, out.as_deref()),
}
```

Each handler is a free function (like `describe`/`verify`, `src/main.rs:39-56`):
read input, call the library, write the rendered grammar to `--out` or stdout,
and `eprintln!` + `std::process::exit(1)` on any `Err` (same pattern as
`verify`, `src/main.rs:47-54`).

### Usage examples (exact)

```bash
# Infer a grammar from a directory of correct example programs, emit LiNo to stdout.
cargo run -- infer examples/json-samples/

# Infer from explicit files, emit GBNF, print D1 metrics to stderr, write to a file.
cargo run -- infer a.txt b.txt c.txt --format gbnf --metrics --out json.gbnf

# Import a BNF grammar into the IR, rendered as LiNo (default).
cargo run -- import-grammar --format bnf grammars/postal.bnf

# Import an EBNF grammar and re-render it as BNF (cross-format round-trip).
cargo run -- import-grammar --format ebnf grammars/expr.ebnf --to bnf

# Emit an IR/LiNo grammar to GBNF for llama.cpp constraint use.
cargo run -- emit-grammar --format gbnf grammars/expr.lino --out expr.gbnf

# Translate a grammar's rule names/comments English -> Russian (structure preserved).
cargo run -- translate-grammar grammars/expr.lino --from-language en --to-language ru
```

### Output formats

- `infer` / `import-grammar` / `emit-grammar` / `translate-grammar` print the
  rendered grammar in the requested notation to stdout (default), or write it to
  `--out <path>`. The default surface is **LiNo** (the project's textual storage
  surface, P-8 — `src/lino_serialization.rs`), matching how `describe` emits
  LiNo-style lines that round-trip through `parse()`/`reconstruct_text()`
  (`README.md` §CLI).
- `infer --metrics` additionally writes a one-line precision/recall/F1/wall-clock
  summary to **stderr** (the D1 metric definitions, [`D1`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/D1-inference-evaluation-harness.md)),
  so stdout stays a clean grammar suitable for piping.
- Errors (parse failure, unsupported format, unreadable file) go to stderr; the
  process exits non-zero (mirrors `verify`, `src/main.rs:47-54`).

## File-level plan

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/main.rs` | Add four `Command` variants + their `match` arms (`src/main.rs:16-37`), the `ValueEnum` arg enums, and the four handler functions modelled on `describe`/`verify` (`src/main.rs:39-56`). |
| `src/lib.rs` | No new public API required if importer/emitter/infer entry points are already re-exported (A1/B1/C1/D5); add a thin `cli` helper module only if shared rendering (IR↔LiNo↔format) warrants it — otherwise keep logic in `main.rs`. |
| `README.md` | Extend §CLI with the four new subcommands + the usage examples above. |
| `tests/integration/mod.rs` | Register CLI integration tests (invoke the built binary via `assert_cmd` or `std::process::Command`). |
| `tests/fixtures/grammar/` | Reuse B1/C1 fixtures; add a tiny example-text corpus for `infer`. |
| `changelog.d/` | Add a fragment (see CONTRIBUTING / `README.md` changelog section). |

## Reuse

- `clap::{Parser, Subcommand}` scaffold + the `describe`/`verify` handler pattern — `src/main.rs:1-56` (copy the enum-variant + free-function + `process::exit(1)` shape). `clap` is already a dependency with the `derive` feature (`Cargo.toml:36`).
- A1 `Grammar` + `GrammarFormat` + LiNo serialisation (`src/lino_serialization.rs`) — render/parse the IR — [`A1`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/A1-grammar-ir.md).
- `import_bnf` (and B2–B7 siblings) — [`B1`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/B1-bnf-importer.md).
- `emit_bnf`/`emit_ebnf`/`emit_abnf` (and C2/C3/C7 siblings) — [`C1`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/C1-bnf-ebnf-abnf-emitters.md).
- `infer_grammar(...)` + D1 metrics — [`D5`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/D5-blackbox-cfg-inference.md), [`D1`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/D1-inference-evaluation-harness.md).
- Cross-language translation entry point — [`C6`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/proposed-issues/C6-concept-aligned-translation.md) (per [`solution-plans.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/a5964ec5bc5846edf0dcf51549f66b2c9be3aa2e/docs/case-studies/issue-93/solution-plans.md) §Epic C, C6 reuses `reconstruct_text_as`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo run -- infer <dir>` reads example texts, runs D5, and prints a
      grammar in the default (LiNo) notation to stdout; `--format gbnf|bnf|…`
      switches the output notation; `--out <path>` writes to a file instead.
- [ ] `cargo run -- infer <files> --metrics` prints precision/recall/F1/wall-clock
      to **stderr** while stdout still carries only the grammar.
- [ ] `cargo run -- import-grammar --format bnf <file>` imports BNF (B1) and prints
      the IR rendered as LiNo; `--to bnf` re-renders via C1 (cross-format path).
- [ ] `cargo run -- emit-grammar --format gbnf <file>` emits GBNF (C3 once landed;
      `bnf`/`ebnf`/`abnf` via C1 are the M5-guaranteed targets).
- [ ] `cargo run -- translate-grammar <file> --from-language en --to-language ru`
      translates the grammar's human-facing surface (C6), preserving structure.
- [ ] Unsupported/not-yet-implemented `--format` values and unreadable inputs
      produce a clear stderr message and a non-zero exit (no panic), mirroring
      `verify` (`src/main.rs:47-54`).
- [ ] `--help` for each subcommand documents every flag and its default.
- [ ] README §CLI lists the four subcommands with the usage examples above.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` (clippy
      `pedantic`/`nursery` are `warn` per `Cargo.toml:103-106`), and
      `cargo test --all-features` all pass; `rust-script scripts/check-no-src-tests.rs`
      passes (tests live under `tests/`, not `src/`).

## Tests

- `tests/integration/` (invoke the built binary, e.g. via `std::process::Command`
  or `assert_cmd`):
  - `infer` over a fixture example-corpus → stdout is a non-empty grammar in the
    requested notation; exit code 0.
  - `infer --metrics` → stderr contains a precision/recall/F1 line; stdout is
    still a valid grammar.
  - `import-grammar --format bnf <fixture.bnf>` → stdout renders the imported IR;
    importing then `--to bnf` yields BNF equivalent to the input (cross-format).
  - `emit-grammar --format bnf <fixture.lino>` → stdout is valid BNF.
  - `translate-grammar … --from-language en --to-language ru` → rule structure
    unchanged, human-facing tokens translated.
  - bad `--format`, missing file, and empty examples each exit non-zero with a
    stderr message and no panic.
- Keep example corpora small and under `tests/fixtures/grammar/`.

## References

- CLI scaffold + handler style: `src/main.rs:1-56`; README §CLI.
- `clap` derive: <https://docs.rs/clap> (already a dependency, `Cargo.toml:36`).
